label: Copy phase from the 3rd output on, weighted by token identity (strongest when outputting n)
explanation: 99.7% of activation mass falls in the copy phase (t > L). It is essentially silent on the original tokens, the <DEL> step, and the first two outputs (recall_idx 0-1). Firing peaks at recall_idx 3-4 (absolute t 11-12) and drops off for later outputs. Inside the copy phase, whether it fires and how strongly depends heavily on token identity. Firing rate is highest when the token being output is n (65% of such steps; the top examples peak on the step just before or while outputting n), followed by e, z, 1, h and f. Some input tokens (h, n, x, i) also raise it. On its own, phase==2 & recall_idx>=2 gives recall 0.99 but precision only 0.27. Adding the token sets raises dev F1 to about 0.57 (mass recall 0.85). The token dependence is graded rather than a clean category, so the description is incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: n, e, z, 1, h, f; least: t, d, p, 3) and the current input token, by step (t=1: t, 2; t=2: t, 2, d, o; t=11: h, n, x, i); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=2, phase=2.
